title: Latency SLO requested — must define an event ratio, not a percentile threshold
code_snippet:
# "We want a latency SLO for the search API: 99% of searches should feel fast.
#  We already export search_request_duration_seconds as a histogram."
# Define the SLI, the SLO, and the alert.
expected_feedback: Define the SLI as the PROPORTION OF REQUESTS FASTER THAN A THRESHOLD, not a percentile value: `sum(rate(search_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.4"}[5m])) / sum(rate(search_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))`, with the SLO stated as '99% of valid searches complete under 400ms over 30 days'. `histogram_quantile(0.99, ...)` returns a duration, so there is no countable bad event and therefore no error budget and no burn rate to alert on; it is also unsafe to average across instances or re-aggregate over time. Keep it for dashboards. Numerator and denominator must come from the SAME histogram with the SAME exclusions -- `le="0.4"` over `_count` (or `le="+Inf"`) -- otherwise the ratio can exceed 1. Also state which events are VALID (exclude health checks, /metrics, client-cancelled requests) and note the instrumentation prerequisite: if the histogram carries no status label, a valid-request latency SLI cannot be computed from it and that limitation must be reported rather than papered over. Alert with a multi-window burn rate against this ratio.
